extracted.intended_audience: general readers of wartime memoir / readers interested in civilian life in Paris during WWI
extracted.subtask_description: Crafting a personal/wartime memoir or literary nonfiction account of civilian life during war, emphasizing lived experience, everyday detail, and factual context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Véridique / truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: "I want to be what the French call _véridique_. This is how we felt during the first winter..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present events and feelings honestly; include the small, everyday impressions and petty difficulties because they reflect how people actually experienced wartime. Emphasize subjective truth about emotions and daily life rather than only grand strategic narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of mundane domestic detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The author repeatedly recounts household troubles (coal rationing, laundry, elevator stoppages, difficulty finding servants, difficulty obtaining groceries) and notes: "Curious it seems to me now... that I find myself penning page after page of the story of petty household difficulties. But I want to be ... véridique. This is how we felt..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, ordinary domestic details (food, heating, clothing, servants, repairs) to ground the memoir and convey the lived reality of wartime. Small anecdotes (e.g., the laundress, Grimes the order-man, burnt toast) serve as representative evidence of broader social conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrative anecdote and dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: The text employs dialogue and monologue (e.g., the long monologue by Grimes; quotes from a dressmaker) to reveal attitudes and social dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quoted speech and extended anecdotes to reveal character, social pressures, and common reasoning. Let representative voices illustrate community beliefs and behaviors rather than relying solely on authorial summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual and factual specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative situates episodes with concrete references to events and measures (e.g., Gotha raids, 'Big Bertha', municipal orders to extinguish lights and close tram/underground services, ABRI placards, allocation of cellar space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear factual context (dates/periods, named phenomena or policies, observable consequences) so readers can understand the scale and nature of wartime disruptions. Use specific examples (local ordinances, types of raids, public responses) to anchor personal recollection in verifiable reality.
